newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Next week good for OLOs but longer term bleak.
newsitem.headline: Next week good for OLOs but longer term bleak.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds are likely to continue their upward correction next week once uncertainty over the outcome of the French elections has evaporated but the longer term outlook is bleak, analysts said on Friday

"Predictions for next week are good but (the rise) is just part of a longer-term topping out which will lead to lower prices in Europe, and in the U.S. to a lower extent," said Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank.
He added he expected European and U.S. markets to disconnect in the summer with the spread widening considerably.
Fieremans said that the wave of U.S. data earlier on Friday had been positive for bond markets on balance.
At 1445 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 6.02 percent against 6.03 percent before the data.

The prospect of the second round of French elections on Sunday and more potential quarrelling between the German government and Bundesbank over Bonn's plans to revaluate gold reserves was mesmerising markets, traders said.
But Fieremans believed the German tit-for-tat and French vote would not lead to a delay of EMU but rather put pressure on European currencies.
"There will be no crisis, otherwise we would have seen something quite different," he said.
The franc, already well above its ERM midpoint of 20.6255, was slightly affected by EMU tension and once again weakened marginally to 20.6455/70 from 20.6435/50 earlier in the day.
